brief: European financial stress intensified as Q4 began, echoing the Euro crisis: the Franco-German 10yr spread and the Italy-bund spread both saw their biggest daily jumps in years, hitting French and Italian equities and banks (Societe Generale, Credit Agricole, BNP Paribas) and widening HY credit spreads to a six-month high. That stress raised doubt the ECB could keep hiking as planned, so December ECB hike pricing fell and German bund yields dropped. Energy added pressure: Brent rose 4.37% to $102.31 after Trump said bombing Iran was possible once midterms passed, and Bloomberg reported a US carrier deployment to the Persian Gulf. In the US, a hawkish data batch (jobless claims at a 10-week low, ISM prices-paid and employment components beating) initially pushed the 10yr Treasury yield to its highest since 2002, but dovish comments from Fed officials Jefferson, Bowman and Williams reversed that, cutting October hike odds to 30% from 70% on Monday; the S&P 500 ended a run of losses. Asian markets fell overnight (Hang Seng, Nikkei) ahead of today's September jobs report, which DB forecasts at +60k versus last month's +162k.
